newsitem.title: USA: Nevada Power sets rate cut, earnings charge.
newsitem.headline: Nevada Power sets rate cut, earnings charge.

text.p: Public Service Commission of Nevada (PSCN) on Thursday approved Nevada Power Co's request to reduce customers' rates by nearly $45 million.
Separately, the commission rendered its decision on a long standing dispute involving various coal contracts, and ordered a one-time reduction in customer rates of around $8 million.
Nevada Power said the decision on the coal matters will result in a reduction in 1996 earnings of approximately 10 cents per common share. The company expects to report its 1996 results mid-February.
The combined effect of the commission decisions is a rate reduction of nearly $53 million.

Residential customers will see a reduction of over $9 million, while public entities such as the Southern Nevada Water Authority and Las Vegas Valley cities will receive $12 million in annual rate reductions.
Medium-sized commercial customers and other large customers will receive a $32 million rate reduction.

"We are pleased that we can lower our customers' rates by the $45 million reduction...We are disappointed that the Commission decided to charge the company's shareholders with nearly $8 million of costs related to the coal contracting, but are pleased that we now have these issues resolved," said Richard Hinckley, general counsel for Nevada Power.
The new rates will become effective February 1, 1997.
